correctness.rationale: The upper-interval argument proves both directions. Every first-write state for four messages must have an upper interval containing all four labels. This forces the four radius-one states at length three, after which the overlaps of the three four-point intervals force the antipodal fibers. The packaged exhaustive verifier enumerates all decoder maps at lengths two and three and reproduces the theorem.

Wolf–Wyner–Ziv–Körner extend WOM capacity questions in several information patterns.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader results concern existence, rate, capacity, and constructions; they do not imply the equality classification of interpretation maps for the exact three-cell four-message instance.

evidence: The preliminary and journal papers give a witness, not an equality-case theorem.
The later canonical-example treatment gives the same witness and parity formula.
The catalogue stores one mapping rather than an exhaustive theorem.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Existence of the Rivest–Shamir decoder does not imply that no nonlinear or differently partitioned decoder exists. The new overlap argument supplies precisely that missing implication.

evidence: The 1982 paper defines one generation-independent interpretation function and gives the parity decoder for the three-cell construction.
The 2012 paper reproduces the same decoder as the canonical example.
OEIS A253548 gives the equivalent two-codebook paper-tape formulation and the standard four-symbol example.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: These sources establish the model equivalence and the canonical construction, but none states that every extendable interpretation function is the antipodal partition.

evidence: The catalogue lists one length-three four-by-four WOM instance and its mapping 0,1,2,3,3,2,1,0.
OEIS records the minimum width three for four symbols and gives the standard example.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Both exact resources support the parameter value and canonical representative, but neither claims to enumerate all generation-independent decoder maps or prove their uniqueness. The new exhaustive census counts all 24 labeled maps.

originality.rationale: The inspected historical and later sources display the canonical decoder but do not state or prove that every valid generation-independent decoder has the antipodal partition. A short-code catalogue stores the same canonical mapping as one known instance but does not claim an exhaustive decoder classification. Targeted published-result searches returned no matching WOM rigidity result.
residual_risks: An unpublished exhaustive search or non-indexed note could have observed the same uniqueness. The checked published and public exact resources do not state it.

value.rationale: The result is a natural complete equality classification of the foundational smallest four-message WOM block. It turns a canonical example into a rigidity theorem, identifies the forced repetition-code coset geometry, and clarifies exactly which part of the construction is unique while leaving encoder choices outside the claim.
